purpose: Routing-impact breakdown of the disagreement safety gate across simulation scenarios. Quantifies which routing transitions the gate causes, using existing cross-tabulation data from model_agreement.json. Does NOT change the real OPS-SAT disagreement analysis.

RF_NOMINAL_GB_NOMINAL_AHEAD.routing_outcome: AUTO_EXECUTE (gate does not fire; both models agree low risk)
RF_NOMINAL_GB_NOMINAL_AHEAD.description: Both models agree on nominal/low-risk state. Automatic execution route is preserved.

RF_NOMINAL_GB_CRITICAL_AHEAD.description: Gate fires: current state appears NOMINAL but 30-min forecast indicates CRITICAL_AHEAD. Automatic route is blocked; case routed to human review.

RF_STANDBY_GB_NOMINAL_AHEAD.routing_outcome: PENDING_APPROVAL (RF already elevated; gate does not fire on non-NOMINAL RF)
RF_STANDBY_GB_NOMINAL_AHEAD.description: RF indicates STANDBY (elevated). Gate condition requires RF=NOMINAL; does not fire. Route determined by RF state alone.

RF_STANDBY_GB_CRITICAL_AHEAD.routing_outcome: ESCALATED or PENDING_APPROVAL (both models agree elevated risk; RF already above NOMINAL)
RF_STANDBY_GB_CRITICAL_AHEAD.description: Both models agree elevated/critical risk. RF is already in STANDBY — route was not AUTO to begin with. Gate does not alter an already-elevated route.

RF_SAFE_MODE_GB_CRITICAL_AHEAD.routing_outcome: ESCALATED (RF in SAFE_MODE; route already maximally conservative; gate does not fire on non-NOMINAL RF)
RF_SAFE_MODE_GB_CRITICAL_AHEAD.description: RF in SAFE_MODE — most conservative route already active. Gate condition not met (RF != NOMINAL).

routing_impact_summary.note: 18.9% of scenarios that would otherwise receive an AUTO route (RF=NOMINAL) are blocked by the gate and redirected to PENDING_APPROVAL.

safety_invariants_verified.no_downgrade: Gate cannot downgrade an already-ESCALATED route to PENDING
safety_invariants_verified.sub_threshold_no_fire: Gate does not fire when p_critical < 0.5
safety_invariants_verified.absent_no_fire: Gate does not fire when model_agreement field is absent
safety_invariants_verified.source: policy_tests.json (10/10 disagreement tests pass, 3 safety invariants verified)

real_opssat_disagreement.note: SEPARATE TRACK — this section is preserved from safety_gate_evaluation.json and is NOT changed.
real_opssat_disagreement.conclusion: Disagreement is not an independently validated anomaly predictor on real OPS-SAT data. Precision = 5.3%; 72 of 76 early-warning cases are false positives.

conclusions.primary_conclusion: Disagreement is not an independently validated anomaly predictor. It is a conservative safety gate that blocks automatic routing when model outputs diverge.
conclusions.gate_effectiveness_in_simulation: 171 of 1,800 simulation test sequences (9.5%) trigger the gate. Of the 905 sequences where RF=NOMINAL, 171 (18.9%) have their AUTO route blocked and redirected to PENDING_APPROVAL.
conclusions.gate_value_on_real_data: The gate's value on real data is not in early-warning precision (5.3%) — it is in preventing AUTO_EXECUTE when models disagree, regardless of ground-truth outcome. This is the intended conservative behavior for a human-in-the-loop system.
conclusions.deterministic_behavior: All routing transitions are deterministic. The gate never overrides a route that is already elevated above AUTO.

limitations: Simulation gate analysis uses a chronological test split (1,800 of 12,000 sequences). Real-world trigger rates are unknown.
Real OPS-SAT segments lack p_critical scores from the simulation forecaster; gate analysis on real data is via binary label disagreement proxy.
5.3% early-warning precision on real OPS-SAT is disclosed and not hidden.
No human operator study of gate utility has been performed.
The routing breakdown is derived from frozen cross-tabulation data — no new model inference.
